exercises.title: A hash map, small enough to read
exercises.task: Read HashMap: a hash function picks a bucket, each bucket is a short list of entries, and the map doubles its buckets when they get too full. Run prints the buckets for a few host names, then shows the map growing.

exercises.title: Write Get and Put
exercises.task: The hash function and the growing are given. Fill Get (look in the key's bucket) and Put (replace the value if the key is there, add an entry otherwise).
hints: Both start the same way: b := m.buckets[m.bucketOf(key)], then a loop over the entries of that one bucket.
Several keys can land in the same bucket: compare the key of each entry, not just take the first one.
In Put, change the value through the index (m.buckets[i][j].value = value): a range variable is a copy.

exercises.title: Count status codes
exercises.task: StatusCounts receives access-log lines like GET /api/users 200 12ms. Return how many times each status code appears, most frequent first (ties: smaller code first). Use a Go map to count, then sort.
hints: strings.Fields(line) splits on spaces; the status is the third field.
Count in a map[string]int, then copy the map into a slice of Count: a map has no order.
sort.Slice(out, func(i, j int) bool { … }): compare N first, then Code.
